$schema: Issue #708 Learn panel content. Keys mirror ViewMode + a few synthetic keys for non-diagram pages.

map.title: Knowledge Map
map.summary: Single-canvas overview composed from services, clusters, APIs, and infrastructure. The fastest way to answer 'what's in this codebase?' on first visit.
map.body: Each node carries a meta.layer accent and a meta.drillDownGraphId. Click any node to drill into the existing layer view (service → L2a feature, cluster → L2b api-list, API → L3 sequence). The overlay panel toggles individual layers + the diff overlay on and off. Domain and Tour overlays are placeholders for #701 / #702 — disabled until those features land per repo.
map.powerExtra: Backed by `mapGraphBuilder.buildMapGraph`. Rebuilt at workspace init, on every cascade event, and on-demand when the panel is opened. The standalone server rebuilds it inside handleRequestRoute when the cache is stale.

domain.title: Business Domains
domain.summary: Verb-action clusters of the codebase — 'Authenticate users', 'Process payments' — that answer 'what does this codebase do?' rather than 'how is it organized?'.
domain.body: Heuristic domain assignment from route-path keywords + Louvain cluster names. Confidence reflects evidence strength: 0.6 for a route match, 0.4 for a cluster-label-only match, 0.2 for the catch-all 'Other' bucket. Inter-domain edges show file overlap so cross-cutting concerns surface immediately.
domain.powerExtra: The 🧠 chip on the Domains card toggles the optional LLM refinement layer on top. Heuristic stays the source of truth; the LLM only renames, recalibrates confidence (capped +0.3 over heuristic), and suggests merges. Refined names persist to the sqlite v9 `domains` table.

feature.title: Feature Areas
feature.summary: Louvain communities over the workspace call graph — clusters of files that call each other often, which usually means they implement a single capability together.
feature.body: Hover any cluster to see its files. Click to drill into the L2b api list (every entry point that belongs to the cluster). The Modules ↔ Domains toggle at the top swaps in the heuristic business-domain clustering on the same canvas.
feature.powerExtra: `featureGraphBuilder.buildFeatureGraph` runs `detectCommunities` (which calls Louvain via `core/analysis/communityDetector.ts`) then diffs against the baseline so additions / removals / membership changes light up. Sub-clusters appear as pills when a cluster exceeds 15 files.

microservice.title: L1 System Design
microservice.summary: Top-level architecture: services (top-level source directories or detected microservices), inter-service calls, and infrastructure (databases / caches / queues / external APIs).
microservice.body: Click a service to drill into its features (L2a). Infrastructure nodes have type discriminators (database / cache / queue / external / sdk) so a glance tells you what kind of dependency a service has on each.
microservice.powerExtra: Built by `microserviceGraphBuilder` — runs `detectServices` + `detectInfrastructureServices` against the snapshot. Workers (jobs + MQ consumers) become sibling nodes via `meta.worker: true`. Service detection reads filesystem each pass; the graph is always re-derived on open instead of cached.

api-list.title: API List (L2b)
api-list.summary: Every entry point in the cluster: HTTP routes, screens, navigation links, background jobs, MQ consumers, CLI commands, push handlers, and more.
api-list.body: Sections collapse by category. The search filter narrows by route, handler name, or method. The `/` key focuses the search box from anywhere on the panel.
api-list.powerExtra: Each item is an `ApiRecord` with a synthetic `method` discriminator: `GET`/`POST`/… for HTTP; `JOB` / `MQ_CONSUMER` / `CLI_COMMAND` / `SCREEN` / `NAV_ROUTE` / `NETWORK` / `DI_BINDING` for non-HTTP. See `frameworkDetector.ts` + `mobile/*.ts` for the full taxonomy.

sequence.title: L3 Sequence Diagram
sequence.summary: Call sequence for one API handler — which participants (modules, classes, external services) interact and in what order.
sequence.body: Participants are inferred from imports + receiver types. Messages are inline from the handler body. Loops and conditionals collapse to repeated arrows; the renderer doesn't pretend to be a full state machine.
sequence.powerExtra: Driven by `sequenceGraphBuilder.buildSequenceGraph`. The BFS depth limit is `codeatlas.sequenceTraversalDepth` (default 8). When a call site can't be resolved (no matching import or LSP fallback), it lands on an `unknown` participant — intentional design choice (see #213).

file.title: L4 File Dependency
file.summary: One file's imports, exports, and dependent files. The L4 layer is the bridge between code-level details and cluster-level overviews.
file.body: Function and class nodes inside the file are also visible. Click a function to open its L5 flow chart.
file.powerExtra: `fileGraphBuilder.buildFileGraph` runs per-file post-cascade. FE/mobile services get additional node kinds (`component`, `hook`, `store`, `fetcher`, `route-config`, `view`, `viewmodel`, `repository`, `network-client`, `persistence`) via the FileGraphEnricher.

flow.title: L5 Function Flow Chart
flow.summary: Control flow inside one function: branches, loops, returns, throws. The deepest layer; use it to pick apart a tricky implementation.
flow.body: Decision nodes render as diamonds; loops as repeated arrows; returns / throws as terminal pills. Edges carry the branch labels (`if`, `else if`, `else`, `for`, …).
flow.powerExtra: Built by `flowGraphBuilder.buildFlowGraph` from the AST. Anonymous arrow handlers attached to routes (Express / Fastify / Hono) get their own flow graphs via the anonymous-route finder.

health.title: Health Report
health.summary: Code health diagnostics: dead code, god files (too many responsibilities), high coupling, dependency cycles, orphaned clusters.
health.body: Each card is severity-colored. Click for the underlying entities. Dead code detection uses the call graph; god-file detection uses LOC + member count.
health.powerExtra: `analyzeHealth` reads from the working snapshot only — no AST pass. Re-runs on every cascade. Per-finding severity thresholds live at the top of `healthAnalyzer.ts`.

screen-content.title: L2b Screen Content
screen-content.summary: What a screen renders + the interactions wired to it. The FE / mobile analogue of the HTTP API list.
screen-content.body: Sections: visual elements (text / button / image / form), interactions (onSubmit / onClick), data hooks (useSWR / useQuery / fetch), navigation outbound (router.push / Link).
screen-content.powerExtra: Driven by `screenContentExtractor`. Populated for services classified as `frontend` or `mobile` via `repoCategories.ts`. Backend services produce zero records here.

tour.title: Onboarding Tour
tour.summary: Guided walkthrough of the codebase, ordered by call-graph fan-in DESC. Designed for a 30-minute first read.
tour.body: Prev / Next steps through entry points one at a time. Each step shows what the route does + which other code calls into it. Switch to 'Recent changes' mode to walk through what's new instead.
tour.powerExtra: `tourBuilder.buildTour` produces the step list. The MCP `get_tour` tool exposes the same data to agents. Future iterations will generate per-step LLM blurbs to replace the heuristic template (#702 follow-up).
